newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi unions protest talks with Hutu rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi unions protest talks with Hutu rebels.

text.p: Burundi's trade unions on Tuesday demanded an end to negotiations between military leader Pierre Buyoya and Hutu rebels.
A total of 23 unions warned Buyoya in a seven-point statement against talks with rebels from the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
"We agree with negotiations between Hutus and Tutsis but only with those who are not killers. We refuse to negotiate with killers," the first point of the statement said.
"We also condemn the procedure of the government which proceeds with negotiations without consulting the people," the statement said.
The unions called on all workers and the population at large to protest against the talks, promising action if they continue.

Ethnic Tutsi Buyoya, who took power in a coup last July, announced last week his government had signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with CNDD after secret talks with CNDD in Rome aimed at ending a bitter civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and rebels.
The announcement sparked protests by university students and Tutsi politicians who fear any power ceded to CNDD compromises their security.
More than 150,000 people have died in Burundi since 1993 when the country's first democratically-elected Hutu president was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.
